# Character Builder — Studio (single pipeline)

**Flow:** 1) generate a 3-view character sheet → 2) *(optional)* inpaint fixes → 3) split into front/left/back views + remove backgrounds → 4) Hunyuan3D-2mv-turbo lifts the three views into one GLB mesh.

**How to run**
1. Edit the green **PROMPT** node in Stage 1. Describe ONE character; keep the turnaround wording.
2. Queue. The full run takes ~8–12 min on the 890M (sheet ~3 min, mesh ~5 min).
3. Meshes land in `output/mesh/`, images in `output/studio/` (also in the **Queue sidebar history**).

**Stage toggles** (STAGE SWITCHES panel, top-left)
- **2 · INPAINT** — off by default. To fix a detail: turn it ON, load the saved sheet into the Stage-2 LoadImage, right-click it → *Open in MaskEditor*, paint over the bad area, write what should be there in the inpaint prompt, re-queue. The Any-Switch automatically feeds the inpainted sheet to Stages 3–4.
- **POSE LOCK** — ON by default (template \	pose_sheet.png\ is installed): every character generates at the exact same 3-view T-pose layout, which is what makes the fixed-thirds cropping in Stage 3 reliable. If the middle view comes out back-facing instead of profile, lower ControlNet strength toward 0.45 so the side-profile text wins — or keep it as an extra back view (the mesh still improves). Regenerate the template anytime with the Helper - Extract Pose Sheet (DWPose) workflow.

**Past generations:** click the Queue tab (sidebar) — every previous output has a thumbnail there. The `studio/` output folder keeps everything on disk.

## LOADERS
Everything below is loaded once and shared by all stages:
- **Z-Image Turbo** (Q5_K_S GGUF) + **Qwen3-4B** encoder + VAE — the 2D stage (9-step distilled → cfg must stay 1.0)
- **BiRefNet** — background removal
- **Hunyuan3D-2mv-turbo** — multi-view image→3D (bundles its own DINOv2 vision encoder + shape VAE)
- **ControlNet Union patch** — pose control for Z-Image (used only when POSE LOCK is on)

## 1 · CHARACTER SHEET
Generates ONE wide image (2304×768) containing the same character three times: **front | left side | back**, T-pose, plain background.
This is the key trick for multi-view 3D on modest hardware: one generation = three consistent views (separate generations would drift).
- Turbo model: keep **9 steps / cfg 1.0 / euler / simple**.
- Reroll the seed until the three views match well — consistency here decides mesh quality.
- **POSE LOCK** group (below) forces the exact same skeleton layout every time via ControlNet, so parts stay swappable between characters.

Character turnaround reference sheet of a single stylized fantasy knight, the exact same character shown three times side by side: front view on the left, left side profile view in the middle, back view on the right, standing in T-pose with arms straight out horizontally, full body head to feet, same low-poly stylized 3D game art style, plain uniform light gray background, soft even studio lighting, no shadows, no text, no labels
nodes.title: PROMPT — describe the character (keep the sheet wording)
Pose CN — STRONG on outer thirds (0.7)
Pose CN — GENTLE on middle (0.35: position only, text decides facing)

## 2 · INPAINT / REFINE  *(off by default — enable in STAGE SWITCHES)*
Fix mistakes without rerolling the whole character:
1. Load the saved sheet (or any view) into the **LoadImage** below.
2. Right-click it → **Open in MaskEditor** → paint over the bad region → Save.
3. Describe what should appear there in the green inpaint prompt.
4. Re-queue. Only the masked area is regenerated (denoise 0.77) and pasted back seamlessly (feathered mask), then flows on to Stages 3–4 automatically via the ACTIVE IMAGE switch.

nodes.title: Sheet to edit → right-click → Open in MaskEditor
INPAINT PROMPT — what should appear in the mask
ACTIVE IMAGE (inpainted if Stage 2 on, else fresh sheet)

## 3 · SPLIT VIEWS + CUTOUT
The active sheet is normalized to 2304×768 and cut into three 768×768 views (front / left / back).
**BiRefNet** masks the character in each view; the cutout is composited onto pure white — exactly what Hunyuan3D wants as input.
The three SaveImage nodes below are your per-view previews; if a view has debris or a bad silhouette, fix it with Stage 2 inpainting before running 3D.

## 4 · IMAGE → 3D (Hunyuan3D-2mv-turbo)
Each white-plate view is encoded by the checkpoint's DINOv2 vision tower, and the **multi-view conditioning** fuses front+left+back into one shape — noticeably sharper backs and sides than single-view.
- Turbo distill: **20 steps / cfg 4.0**.
- `octree_resolution` 256 = default; 384 = hero quality (slower).
- GLB lands in `output/mesh/` — the SaveGLB node shows a live 3D preview you can orbit right here.
- Clean-up + Unreal export: run `blender_export_unreal.py` (see README).

## 4b · TRELLIS 2 HERO  *(off by default — enable in STAGE SWITCHES)*
Sends the FRONT view to the local **trellis.cpp** server (TRELLIS.2-4B, Vulkan on the 890M)
and returns a **fully textured PBR mesh** — higher fidelity than stage 4, at minutes-to-tens-of-minutes cost.
1. Start the server first: `C:\Users\rapiular\Tools\trellis.cpp\start_trellis_server.ps1`
2. Enable this group in STAGE SWITCHES, queue.
- 512 = draft (~5-10 min), 1024 = hero (~15-30 min).
- Keep `bg_removal=threshold` (inputs are already on white; the in-server BiRefNet needs a
  >2 GiB buffer that this iGPU driver's per-allocation limit rejects).
